Merit for admission in the University may be determined either on the basis of marks or grade obtained in the qualifying examination and achievements in co-curricular and extra-curricular activities or on the basis of marks or grade obtained in the entrance test conducted at State level either by the University or an association of the Universities conducting similar courses or by any agency of the State Government. dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956

Key Provisions:
1.	Establishment of Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) 
o	The Act established the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) as a statutory body. 
o	LIC was granted legal status as a corporate entity with perpetual succession and a common seal. 
o	It was empowered to acquire property, enter into contracts, and undertake legal proceedings. 
2.	Transfer of Life Insurance Business 
o	The Act provided for the transfer and vesting of the life insurance business of existing insurers in LIC. 
o	Private life insurance companies operating in India were nationalised, and their assets and liabilities were transferred to LIC. 
3.	Functions of LIC
LIC was responsible for: 
o	Carrying on life insurance business. 
o	Developing and expanding life insurance services across India. 
o	Conducting business with the objective of serving policyholders. 
o	Investing funds in accordance with government-approved policies. 
4.	Management and Administration 
o	The Act provided for the constitution of the LIC Board and appointment of the Chairman and members by the Central Government. 
o	It defined the powers and duties of the Corporation and its governing authorities. 
5.	Financial Provisions 
o	LIC was required to maintain proper accounts and prepare annual reports. 
o	The accounts were subject to audit and review by prescribed authorities. 
o	The Corporation was required to submit reports to the Central Government. 
6.	Protection of Policyholders 
o	The Act aimed to safeguard the interests of life insurance policyholders by placing the insurance business under public ownership and supervision. 
7.	Power to Make Rules and Regulations 
o	The Central Government was empowered to make rules for implementing the provisions of the Act. 
o	LIC was authorised to make regulations relating to its internal functioning and business operations.

(1) The Commandant or any other authority or officer as may be prescribed, may, subject to any rules made under this Act, award in lieu of, or in addition to, suspension or dismissal any one or more of the following punishments to any member of the Force whom he considers to be guilty of disobedience, neglect of duty, or remissness in the discharge of any duty or of other misconduct in his capacity as a member of the Force, that is to say,—
(a) reduction in rank;
(b)fine of any amount not exceeding one month's pay and allowances;
(c) confinement to quarters, lines or camp for a term not exceeding one month;
(d) confinement in the quarter-guard for not more than twenty-eight days, with or without punishment drill or extra guard, fatigue or other duty; and
(e) removal from any office of distinction or special emolument in the Force.
(2) Any punishment specified in clause (c) or clause (d) of sub-section (1) may be awarded by any gazetted officer when in command of any detachment of the Force away from headquarters, provided he is specially authorised in this behalf by the Commandant.
(3) The assistant commandant, a company officer or a subordinate officer, not being below the rank of subedar or inspector, commanding a separate detachment or an outpost, or in temporary command at the headquarters of the Force, may, without a formal trial, award to any member of the Force who is for the time being subject to his authority any one or more of the following punishments for the commission of any petty offence against discipline which is not otherwise provided for in this Act, or which is not of a sufficiently serious nature to require prosecution before a criminal Court, that is to say,—

(c) any investigation, legal proceedings or remedy in respect of such penalty, forfeiture or punishment and any such penalty, forfeiture or punishment may be imposed as if this Act had not been passed.
(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), all notifications, rules, regulations, orders, directions, and powers made, issued or conferred under the provisions of the 2Telangana District Police Act, 1329 F. and in force at the commencement of this Act, shall so far as they are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act continue to be in force in the Cyberabad Metropolitan Area, until they are replaced by the notification, rules, regulations, orders, directions and powers to be made or issued or conferred under this Act.
